selected.assay: bulk RNA-seq (TruSeq stranded total RNA, NextSeq500), leg subcutaneous adipose tissue
selected.primary_estimand: Within-subject change in adipose-tissue gene expression after one acute 30-min cycling bout (85% HRmax), at 0 min post-exercise (POST) and 3 h recovery (REC) versus pre-exercise basal (PRE), separately in NGT (n=20) and T2D (n=28) participants
selected.sample_inclusion: 20 NGT (11M/9F) + 28 T2D (16M/12F) participants, three biopsies each (S2.1.p1, TAB1)
planned_contrasts: NGT POST vs PRE (S2.1.p1; paper: 712 DEGs)
T2D POST vs PRE (S2.1.p1; paper: 893 DEGs)
NGT REC vs PRE (S2.1.p1; count not stated exactly; T2D REC has 3228 genes not shared with NGT REC, implying 1088 shared)
T2D REC vs PRE (S2.1.p1; paper: 4316 DEGs)
T2D vs NGT at PRE (S2.1.p1; 589 DEGs; basal disease comparison, not an exercise contrast)
selected.paper_method: edgeR filterByExpr (min.count 15, design ~0+group+sex); limma with quality weights (voomWithQualityWeights implied) on ~0 + group + sex, duplicateCorrelation blocking on participant (S4.4.2.p1)
selected.paper_results: OSM among most induced post-exercise in both groups; CYR61(CCN1), CXCL2, HBEGF, IL6, COX2(PTGS2) highly induced post; SFRP4 and MXRA5 up at REC in T2D; PPARG down at REC in T2D only; LEP/ADIPOQ/RARRES2 decreased at REC

decisions.reason: S4.4.2.p1 gives filter, model (~0 + group + sex, quality weights, duplicateCorrelation on participant) and threshold (FDR 0.05, 'fold change cut-off of 0.1'); S2.1.p1 gives the per-group counts. 'Fold change cut-off of 0.1' is read as |logFC| > 0.1 on the limma log2 scale (a linear fold change of 0.1 is meaningless as a symmetric cutoff).

checks: TAB2 key resources and S4.4.2.p1 name GSE198922
GEO contact Lundell (L.S.L. did bioinformatics, S5.1.p1), Karolinska
48 participants (20 NGT/28 T2D) and sexes match the paper

Matrix columns (e.g. 11_POST) equal GEO title for 143/144 samples; 1_POST has metadata but no matrix column (missing from the deposited matrix). Time comes from the title suffix, which matches characteristics exercise.

selected.source: GEO data_processing: 'processed.data.csv contains cpm'; values non-integer, column sums ~0.7-7e6
selected.paper_input: raw featureCounts counts into limma with quality weights (voom)

decisions.reason: data_processing explicitly states CPM; 97% non-integer values; no raw counts deposited (supplementary_file NONE besides processed CPM). Raw counts cannot be recovered without library sizes, so voom cannot run as in the paper.

selected.analysis_type: repeated-measures time course within diagnosis strata
selected.estimand_type: causal within-subject (pre/post, no non-exercise control arm)

decisions.reason: S2.1.p1/FIG1B: exercise contrasts are POST vs PRE and REC vs PRE within NGT and within T2D. Repeated biopsies per participant require the participant as blocking unit. Diagnosis is a stratum so time contrasts never cross groups.

covariates.name: sex
covariates.disposition: nested: constant within subject, absorbed by the subject fixed effect

decisions.reason: Paper blocks participants with duplicateCorrelation and adjusts sex (S4.4.2.p1). Here subject is a fixed effect within each stratum; sex is subject-level so it is absorbed. Within-subject time contrasts are identified.

selected.method: limma (moderated t, eBayes) on log2(CPM+1), subject fixed effect

paper_route.method: limma-voom with quality weights, ~0 + group + sex, duplicateCorrelation(participant)
paper_route.reason: only CPM deposited (no raw counts / library sizes for voom); executor has no duplicateCorrelation or array quality weights

deviations: log2(CPM+1) limma instead of voomWithQualityWeights on counts
subject fixed effect instead of duplicateCorrelation random block
separate fit per diagnosis stratum instead of one pooled model (residual variance not shared across groups)
no additional filterByExpr: deposited CPM matrix is used as filtered by the authors

decisions.reason: Matrix-method policy: linear normalized values go to limma after log2. Subject fixed effects give the same within-subject estimand as duplicateCorrelation blocking for time contrasts.
